cases.title: Attributing 'chowkidar chor hai' findings to the Supreme Court
cases.speaker: Rahul Gandhi
cases.original_language: Hindi/English mixed; exact uninterrupted verbatim transcript pending
cases.medium: remarks to media after Rafale admissibility order
cases.claim_text: Court-recorded description: Rahul Gandhi attributed to the Supreme Court the view that 'Chowkidar (Mr. Narendra Modi, Prime Minister) is a thief'. This is not labeled a verbatim recording transcript.
testable_propositions: The Supreme Court judicially found or endorsed the assertion that Narendra Modi was a thief or guilty of Rafale corruption.
cases.confidence: high on the narrow proposition; original full recording remains to be authenticated
evidence_for: Contemporaneous recorded-video page establishes an attribution was publicly reported; judgment itself describes the attribution.
The 10 April ruling really did dismiss the Union's document-admissibility objection, as confirmed by the judgment text and contemporaneous Ministry of Defence PIB statement.
evidence_against: 15 Apr 2019 Supreme Court order explicitly disclaimed any such finding, limiting the 10 Apr decision to admissibility of documents.
14 Nov 2019 judgment paras 26-33 records attribution, unconditional apology on 8 May, and closure with caution.
Authenticated SC original 15 Apr 2019 PDF expressly rules out the alleged judicial finding; independently archived Nov 2019 judgment PDF paras 26-33 inspected.
Newly inspected 10 April 2019 Supreme Court judgment reproduction, majority paragraph 12 (printed p.18), directly limits the ruling to documentary admissibility and future review on merits.

Supreme Court's own 10 Apr 2019 judgment now directly retrieved from api.sci.gov.in: operative majority para 12 on PDF page 18 explicitly leaves review merits for later adjudication; it supplies no judicial finding of theft.
cases.counterargument: Gandhi described his rhetoric as heat-of-campaign and said the attribution was unintentional. That speaks to intent, not truth of the attributed judicial finding.
limitations: 15 Apr order and 10 Apr substantive admissibility judgment both retrieved from official Supreme Court host; judiciary-hosted 14 Nov judgment remains inaccessible, but its third-party PDF reproduction has been inspected
Whole April 10 recording and surrounding remarks not transcribed
No broader verdict here on merits of the Rafale corruption allegations
Contemporaneous video URL identified with secondary timestamp 03:05–03:18 but playback and full context not validated
New 10 Apr 2019 Economic Times publisher recording URL identified; full original video still not played or transcribed
cases.next_action: Authenticate full unedited 10 April 2019 Rahul Gandhi remarks and Hindi/English timecoded transcript; retrieve court-domain 14 Nov 2019 final judgment directly; seek human editorial review. Keep publication status draft.

cases.title: Mahadevapura: 1,00,250 allegedly stolen votes
cases.speaker: Rahul Gandhi
cases.original_language: English, based on Congress summary; full unedited video verification pending
cases.medium: press conference, Indira Bhawan, New Delhi
cases.claim_text: Congress-edited highlights: 'approximately 1,00,250 votes were stolen out of 6.5 lakh total votes in Mahadevapura.'
cases.claim_type: quantitative electoral fraud and causal allegation
testable_propositions: Exactly or approximately 100,250 fraudulent ballots were cast or counted in 2024.
Five categories of suspicious electoral roll entries reliably identify unique ineligible voters rather than overlapping entries or stale address records.
The suspicious entries caused the result in Bangalore Central to change.
BJP and ECI intentionally colluded in this alleged manipulation.
cases.confidence: moderate on failure to establish ballot theft, not a finding that rolls were clean
evidence_for: Independent field checks found mass registrations tied to changing-tenancy addresses; irregular/stale entries have support.
Five category totals supplied by Congress sum to 100,250, but arithmetic is not independent verification.
2024 ECI source records 659826 registered Mahadevapura electors, compatible with 6.5 lakh as roll denominator, but not 6.5 lakh ballots cast.
Rahul Gandhi's first-party public channel links the contemporaneous full press conference recording, creating a path to contextual claim authentication; the recording was not played.

Claimant-controlled website 31 Aug 2025 newsletter search-indexed infographic repeats the five categories and numbers. This corroborates publication of the claim, not individual electoral anomalies or illegal ballots.
evidence_against: An entry in a voter roll is not proof that a ballot was cast; no identified voter-level ballot reconciliation or deduplicated methodology retrieved.
Mobility and legitimate historic occupancy explain some high address counts, while not dispelling stale/ineligible entries.
CEO Karnataka asked for a sworn particulars-based complaint, which is an institutional response rather than proof of falsity.
ECI segment table reports only 354830 EVM votes (including NOTA) for Mahadevapura; 6.5 lakh is elector count, not EVM ballots polled.
ECI indexed constituency result reports BJP 658915 versus INC 626208, winning margin 32707; changing this margin cannot be inferred from 100250 suspicious entries without proven unique invalid votes.

10 Aug 2025 CEO Karnataka social notice, as quoted by independent contemporary reports, contests one purported instance of double voting; this is an institutional allegation pending review of its inquiry and underlying marked-roll evidence, not independently proven exculpatory evidence.

Rule 49L requires voter entry in Form 17A and a marked roll; rule 93 restricts access to the authenticated sealed records. Neither an image of two alleged ticked entries nor duplicate registrations alone proves two cast votes.

ECI August 2023 EVM manual and 15 July 2025 ECI FAQ describe Form 17C as the polling-station total vote account. Form 17A attendance differs in concept from EVM ballots polled, so any claimed double-voting count must be independently reconciled.

An August 2025 video statement attributed to the voter denies double voting, as reported by India Today. Source video and original Form 17A/marked electoral roll not inspected; testimony should be weighed, not treated as an official final adjudication.
limitations: Constituency 2024 source voter roll and supplemental logs not retrieved
Full 7 August 2025 claimant-owned press conference URL recovered and linked from first-party channel, but full audio/video and claim timestamps not checked
